title: Best Contact Center AI Solutions for Telephony Integration (2026 Ranked Guide)
summary: Ask a voice AI vendor about integration and you usually get a logo wall. Ask which dialer they connect to, whether transfers keep context, and where the disposition lands, and the answers thin out fast. That is the test we ran here. Eight platforms, ranked on named telephony support, pricing you can actually add up, and how they hand a call to a person.
body_markdown:
## TL;DR


- SigmaMind AI ranks first under this guide’s telephony-weighted criteria because it publishes VICIdial setup instructions for adding AI without replacing the dialer. Its reported Five9, NICE, and Genesys connections and CRM workflows require deployment-specific verification.
- SigmaMind AI advertises a $0.04 per-minute platform fee, with speech, model, and carrier costs charged separately. It says it does not charge concurrency fees. Buyers should confirm the current rates and total campaign cost.
- Retell AI is a developer-first alternative for teams prepared to configure and maintain their own integrations. Vapi offers programmable workflows, PolyAI focuses on multilingual enterprise deployments, and Bland AI offers outbound calling tools. Synthflow AI offers a no-code builder, Regal supports event-driven outreach, and Replicant offers a managed service.
- The ranking weighs named telephony connections and CRM data flow. It also considers handoffs and pricing transparency. General feature breadth carries less weight because a voice agent must work with the buyer’s call routing and data flows.


## Why telephony integration depth is the right lens for ranking contact center AI


Telephony integration determines whether a voice agent can operate inside your existing call flow. A dialer sends call audio and signaling to the AI through a SIP trunk or platform connector. The AI handles the conversation and may transfer qualified or escalated callers to an agent. Returning dispositions or lead updates through an API requires a configured data workflow; an audio connection alone does not provide one. SigmaMind AI’s[VICIdial documentation](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/vicidial-integration) explains how VICIdial dials calls and routes them to the AI. Confirm the documented handoff and outcome-logging behavior against the proposed configuration; the audio connection alone does not establish CRM writeback or a context-preserving transfer.


Named-platform support is useful only when you can establish what the proposed connector does for routing, transfers, and data exchange.[Genesys Cloud CX connects to Salesforce](https://www.genesys.com/capabilities/cloud-and-salesforce) through a prebuilt screen-pop integration, while[NICE CXone ships a dedicated Salesforce agent app](https://www.nice.com/products/crm-integrations/salesforce) and[Five9 integrates natively with Salesforce, ServiceNow, and Microsoft Dynamics](https://www.five9.com/products/capabilities/crm-integration/salesforce) . Authentication, screen-pop timing, and call-record formats vary by connector, so a generic "CRM integration" claim does not establish how a particular handoff works. A generic SIP connection may carry audio but still fail to update a campaign record or preserve context during a warm transfer. Whether your contact center uses VICIdial, Five9, NICE, or Genesys, you should verify the exact connection method and test transfers under real queue conditions. Ask each vendor to show how its SIP connection, post-call data delivery, and human handoffs work in your configuration.


Conversation quality and feature counts matter, but this ranking gives greater weight to dialer connectivity, CRM data flow, handoffs, and disclosed costs. Those criteria overlook whether the software connects to your dialer and writes accurate CRM fields. The software must also support your expected call volume. Pricing deserves the same scrutiny. Per-minute rates and concurrency charges can change operating costs. Telephony fees and implementation costs can do the same even when two agents sound equally capable. A useful ranking therefore examines named integrations and pricing disclosure. Conversation quality remains a separate consideration.


## 1. SigmaMind AI — Best for telephony integration and lead qualification in high-volume call centers


SigmaMind AI ranks first under this guide’s telephony-weighted criteria because its[VICIdial implementation guide](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/vicidial-ai-voice-agent-integration-guide) describes adding a voice agent without replacing the dialer. This is a ranking based on published information, not a claim that the platforms underwent hands-on testing. SigmaMind AI reports support for Five9, NICE, and Genesys and describes API connections to CRMs and internal systems; buyers should verify the available connection and data flow for each deployment. In the documented VICIdial bolt-on approach, VICIdial retains dialing, campaign records, routing rules, and existing reports. Buyers evaluating the reported Five9, NICE, and Genesys support should confirm what remains in place for their own configuration.


In SigmaMind AI’s[published VICIdial implementation guide](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/vicidial-ai-voice-agent-integration-guide) , VICIdial bridges answered outbound calls to the AI through a Remote Agent while retaining campaign control. The published guide specifies a full Remote Extension dial string, including the carrier prefix and registered destination number. For that configuration, check that the agent shows Ready and that its Routing Extension matches the campaign. A separate Remote Agent for each campaign permits a focused pilot without rerouting unrelated campaigns. The[SIP trunk connection steps](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/vicidial-integration) describe a related setup task, not a substitute for checking the Remote Agent routing. Disposition and lead-field updates require a configured integration rather than following automatically from SIP connectivity.


SigmaMind AI lists its platform fee separately from other voice-call costs.[Pay-as-you-go pricing](https://sigmamind.ai/) starts with a $0.04 per-minute platform fee, then adds speech recognition and voice generation. Language model usage and telephony are also billed where applicable. Request a current quote for speech recognition, voice generation, and language model usage because these charges depend on the selected providers and plan. Ask SigmaMind AI which speech, voice, and model providers are available for your deployment, then compare their language support, latency, and combined cost.


SigmaMind AI says it does not charge a separate concurrency fee. Confirm the campaign’s total cost and capacity limits before projecting spending at higher call volumes. For BPO campaigns, ask SigmaMind AI whether the proposed plan provides separate client workspaces, usage tracking, and billing.


BPOs and high-volume contact centers should pilot one campaign and check routing, audio, recording, transfer success, dispositions, and rollback. For VICIdial, confirm SIP registration, codec and NAT compatibility, firewall rules, and trunk and Asterisk channel capacity before scaling. Confirm how the proposed transfer handles the carrier connection and caller ID. A direct transfer alone does not establish that the human agent receives AI qualification notes. That requires additional work, such as mapping qualification data to lead fields and configuring a CRM screen pop.


## 2. Retell AI — Best for developer-first voice agent deployment


Retell AI is a developer-first option for teams that want to build and control voice agents through APIs. Retell AI describes Twilio and Vonage telephony, a HubSpot app, Salesforce API connections, and[other CRM and telephony options](https://www.retellai.com/blog/voice-ai-integrations-crm-telephony-stack) . Ask Retell AI to identify the documented connection method for Genesys, Five9, Amazon Connect, or Avaya in your configuration. Your developers may need to configure authentication, routing, webhooks, and CRM data flows.


Usage-based pricing gives developers control over cost during testing and gradual deployment. Retell charges for voice agents by the second without rounding, and published rates range between[$0.07 and $0.31 per minute](https://www.retellai.com/pricing) . Your selected language model and voice affect the price. The telephony provider and optional services add further costs. Confirm the included concurrent-call allowance and any additional capacity charges on Retell AI’s current plan before estimating deployment costs.


Retell works best when your developers can connect the telephony, model, and CRM services into an operating workflow. HubSpot offers a more packaged connection, but Salesforce actions and some telephony configurations require API or SIP work. You should also confirm static IP support and transfer behavior for older PBXs before committing. If you need predefined dialer workflows, compare the implementation work required by Retell AI and SigmaMind AI in your own contact center configuration.


## 3. Vapi — Best for custom-built voice workflows with developer control


Vapi suits developers who want direct control over call logic and model selection. The platform also lets them trigger real-time API actions and combine speech recognition, language models, voice providers, and telephony services into custom workflows. Flow Studio supports basic prototypes, while complex validation and branching usually require code.


Vapi charges about $0.05 per minute for orchestration alone. Speech recognition and language model usage are billed separately. Voice generation is another charge, as are phone numbers and carrier usage. A[third-party estimate of Vapi costs](https://www.lindy.ai/blog/vapi-ai) puts combined usage at $0.07 to $0.25 or more per minute, depending on provider selection. Request current component rates before using that estimate in a budget. You need to track several provider bills when estimating campaign costs.


Telephony coverage also depends on your selected providers. Check Vapi’s current number availability and whether your target countries require an external telephony provider. According to a[Retell comparison of Vapi and Retell](https://www.retellai.com/blog/retell-vs-vapi) , CRM connections require custom API development rather than native connectors. You should verify that limitation directly during evaluation because the claim comes from a competitor.


Before choosing Vapi, estimate the engineering time required to build, monitor, and maintain telephony and CRM integrations. Your staff will own that work when using its programmable orchestration.


## 4. PolyAI — Best for large multilingual enterprise deployments


PolyAI suits large enterprises that need one voice platform across multiple markets. A[Retell comparison of PolyAI alternatives](https://www.retellai.com/blog/polyai-alternatives-compared) reports that the platform supports more than 45 languages and interruption-friendly conversations; buyers should verify current coverage with PolyAI because the source is a competitor. Ask PolyAI to document which contact center, CRM, payment, and knowledge-source connections Agent Studio supports in the proposed deployment. Ask PolyAI to demonstrate which customer-record, ticketing, payment, and context-preserving transfer actions its proposed integrations support.


PolyAI uses enterprise sales rather than a published self-serve rate card, so request a quote and implementation schedule before comparing it with self-serve software. PolyAI does not publish a self-serve rate card. A[Quiq estimate of PolyAI pricing](https://quiq.com/blog/poly-ai-pricing/) suggests contracts can start around $150,000 per year, but only a PolyAI quote can establish the price for your deployment. Pricing varies with call volume and conversation complexity. Integration work can raise it further. Custom SIP configurations and some managed integrations also require coordination with a PolyAI account manager.


PolyAI works best when multilingual coverage and managed enterprise deployment outweigh fast experimentation or predictable pricing. If you need a quick pilot, ask PolyAI for a proposed start date and production schedule.


## 5. Bland AI — Best for regulated-industry outbound campaigns


Bland AI may fit regulated outbound programs if its security controls and required agreements meet your requirements. A[Lindy review of Bland AI](https://www.lindy.ai/blog/bland-ai-review/) describes SOC 2 controls and HIPAA and GDPR support; obtain Bland AI’s own documentation and verify the scope of its controls, agreements, and configurations. Healthcare buyers should determine whether Bland AI and every applicable subcontractor will sign the required Business Associate Agreements and support their protected-health-information controls. Insurance and financial-services buyers should assess the separate rules governing their campaigns.


Twilio and SIP support let you bring your own telephony provider and route calls through existing infrastructure. Bland AI also provides APIs and webhooks. You can use them to create conditional call flows for custom routing. However, the reviewed sources do not document native integrations with VICIdial, Five9, NICE, or Genesys. Contact centers using those platforms may need custom integration work.


Bland AI combines subscription charges with several usage fees. Depending on the plan, connected calls cost roughly[11 to 14 cents per minute](https://emitrr.com/blog/bland-ai-pricing/) , while outbound attempts incur a minimum charge even when nobody answers. Transfers through Bland numbers and inbound or outbound SMS cost extra. Ask Bland AI whether using Twilio changes transfer charges on the proposed plan. Call volume and transfer activity can still affect the total. Messaging and add-ons can increase it further. If you value predictable monthly costs, you may prefer a simpler per-minute model.


## 6. Synthflow AI — Best for no-code deployment by nontechnical teams


Synthflow AI suits small businesses and agencies that want to launch voice agents without writing code. Its visual builder handles calls that involve appointment booking or lead qualification, while APIs and webhooks connect external services. Complex CRM or scheduling workflows may still require tools such as Zapier or Make, along with Calendly or Cal.com.


Pay-as-you-go pricing lowers the initial commitment. The voice engine costs $0.09 per minute, with separate charges for the language model and managed telephony. A[third-party Synthflow AI pricing estimate](https://zeeg.me/en/blog/post/synthflow-ai-pricing) puts usage at about $0.11 to $0.16 per minute before optional services. Verify current rates and the components included in your quote. Low-latency options may cost extra.


High-volume contact centers face two limits. Check the current pay-as-you-go concurrent-call allowance and the price of additional capacity before sizing a large queue. Synthflow’s public materials do not document native connections to VICIdial, Five9, NICE, or Genesys. Synthflow offers unlimited concurrency and native telephony through its custom Enterprise plan, but buyers must contact the company for pricing. For large queues on an existing dialer, compare Synthflow AI’s proposed concurrency allowance, connection method, and total cost with the custom Enterprise plan.


## 7. Regal — Best for outbound event-driven engagement in insurance and financial services


Regal fits insurance and financial services companies that organize outbound calls around customer events. Its no-code Journey Builder can trigger multi-step outreach after events such as a missed payment or form submission. Ask Regal to demonstrate how an AI call triggers human follow-up and what conversation context the agent receives during a transfer.


Ask Regal to demonstrate its TCPA- and TSR-related settings, including quiet hours, opt-out management, audit logs, and branded caller ID. Your legal staff should confirm that the proposed configuration meets the rules for each campaign. Ask Regal to demonstrate how its Salesforce and HubSpot connections trigger calls and write outcomes to the correct CRM records. Support the named connections with Regal’s published integration documentation rather than the current third-party link.


Regal is better suited to structured engagement flows than to broad customer support. Open-ended, multichannel support across voice, chat, and email may require additional configuration or software. Regal does not publicly document integrations with VICIdial, Five9, NICE, or Genesys, so you should confirm how calls and handoffs connect to the contact center’s current dialer.


Quote-based pricing creates another evaluation step. Regal does not publish per-minute rates or standard tiers, and deployment commonly involves a sales-led proof of concept. When comparing contact center AI software, request a full estimate that includes usage and concurrency costs. The estimate should also cover compliance requirements and integration work.


## 8. Replicant — Best for large enterprises prioritizing call containment over configurability


Replicant suits large contact centers that want a vendor-managed service focused on call containment. A[Retell comparison of Replicant, PolyAI, and Voiceflow](https://www.retellai.com/blog/retell-vs-polyai-vs-replicant-vs-voiceflow) describes Replicant’s Replicare offering as a managed service with an annual fee. Ask Replicant which deployment, maintenance, flow-development, and tuning work its proposal includes.


Confirm which telephony and CCaaS connection Replicant proposes for your stack, whether direct BYOC SIP is available, and who can change call flows after launch. A partner connection may reduce integration work, but its effect on deployment time and developer control depends on the agreement.


Replicant’s cost and delivery model limits its fit for smaller or faster-moving contact centers. Request a Replicant quote, delivery schedule, and change-management terms. A[competitor’s discussion of Replicant implementations](https://thoughtly.com/blog/best-replicant-alternatives-voice-ai) describes lengthy services-led deployments, but it does not establish the price or timeline of your project. If you need self-service configuration or rapid testing, consider a more configurable platform.

## Contact center AI for healthcare: compliance and integration requirements


Industry-specific requirements can change the general shortlist. In healthcare, buyers should evaluate every service that handles protected health information. A patient call may pass through the carrier and speech recognition provider. It may also pass through the language model, voice generator, and contact center AI platform.[Each provider that handles PHI may need to sign its own Business Associate Agreement](https://telnyx.com/resources/hipaa-compliant-voice-ai-agents) . Map every provider that handles protected health information so you can assess its agreement, access controls, and retention terms.


If an appointment agent must book visits during a call, its EHR connection needs the permissions and data flows to do more than export records afterward. For example, an appointment agent needs permission to check availability, verify the caller, book the visit, and write the result back to Epic, Cerner, or athenahealth. Buyers should test bidirectional API access and failure handling before approving a production deployment.


Audit and retention controls should cover recordings, transcripts, model activity, and EHR API calls. Ask where each vendor processes voice data, who can access transcripts, and whether the platform supports configurable retention periods or zero-retention options. Automated tests should also check for unsafe behavior, such as revealing medication details before identity verification.


Providers using Five9, NICE, or Genesys can include SigmaMind AI in a shortlist, but should verify its reported connection for their configuration before treating it as an established healthcare deployment option. SigmaMind AI’s BAA availability, subcontractor coverage, retention controls, and EHR integration depth still require confirmation during procurement. Bland AI warrants consideration for its stated HIPAA posture. Retell AI and Vapi may suit healthcare providers with engineering resources if all applicable service providers can meet the buyer’s agreement and data-handling requirements. Compare finalists on infrastructure ownership, bidirectional EHR APIs, audit trails, and retention controls rather than accepting a general HIPAA claim.


## Contact center AI for insurance: claims intake and compliance-first evaluation


For insurance agencies with high-volume prospecting or claims calls, an always-available voice agent can collect details before routing a caller to licensed staff. Measure your own response times and abandoned inquiries before projecting gains. A voice agent can immediately capture quote details or collect first-notice-of-loss information, including the policy, incident, and people involved, before routing the record to staff.


Insurance automation requires strict limits on what the AI can decide. Check the[NAIC Model Bulletin](https://content.naic.org/insurance-topics/artificial-intelligence) and applicable state requirements when setting human-review rules for consequential underwriting and claims decisions. State departments of insurance may also require defensible contact logs, recording consent, retention controls, and licensing disclosures. A suitable agent should identify itself as AI and avoid giving coverage advice or making statements that bind coverage. It should transfer those questions to licensed staff.


Agency management system connectivity determines whether intake data becomes useful. Require vendors to demonstrate field-level writeback into Applied Epic, Vertafore AMS360, or EZLynx rather than cite a generic API. Have the vendor demonstrate authorized record creation or updates, transcript handling, the appropriate claims or quote workflow, and an audit trail. Test whether the proposed dialer connection preserves routing and passes the necessary context to a human agent. Verify agency-system writeback separately. For insurers using VICIdial, SigmaMind AI documents an approach that retains the dialer. Insurers using Five9, NICE, or Genesys should first validate its reported connection and separately test any agency-system writeback.


## Contact center AI for retail and e-commerce: phone-support overflow


Retailers with substantial phone volume can evaluate voice AI for promotion-driven overflow, after-hours calls, store-hours questions, and routing callers to the correct location. Measure your own call mix before estimating savings. Use your call records and pilot results to estimate containment and cost per resolved call for your operation.


A multi-location phone agent needs the correct store’s hours and routing rules. It should answer product-availability questions only if authorized, location-specific inventory access and freshness checks have been verified. When the data cannot be trusted, route the caller to a person.


For retailers using VICIdial, SigmaMind AI documents a bolt-on voice-agent route. It also reports Five9, NICE, and Genesys support, which retailers should validate in their own environments. Compare Retell AI, PolyAI, and Vapi on the proposed phone connection and human handoff. Require a demonstration of authorized data access, location-specific answers, and context passed to staff; do not assume an API connection provides live order or inventory data.


## How to choose based on your telephony stack


If you run VICIdial, decide whether to add AI to existing campaigns or migrate away from the dialer. The documented bolt-on route keeps VICIdial’s campaign controls and reports but adds a SIP/media boundary and calls for capacity, transfer, and data-flow testing. A full migration may consolidate operations, but requires re-creating campaign logic, carrier connections, compliance procedures, historic data links, and reports. For a bolt-on pilot, test one campaign’s Remote Agent routing and verify any disposition or lead updates separately; do not assume SIP connectivity writes them back.


If you use Five9, NICE, or Genesys, SigmaMind AI is a candidate for evaluation based on its reported support, not a verified fit for every configuration. Ask each vendor to demonstrate transfer behavior and CRM writeback in your configuration; the published VICIdial steps do not establish how Five9, NICE, or Genesys handles either. PolyAI and Replicant may suit enterprises that prefer a managed deployment, but you should verify support for their exact platform and configuration.


If you have no existing telephony stack, Retell AI and Vapi provide flexible building blocks for a custom deployment, while Synthflow AI offers a simpler no-code route for lower-volume operations. Compare the complete cost of telephony, speech services, language model usage, and concurrency before choosing.


Build a shortlist around your current telephony platform and pilot realistic calls at your expected volume. Check routing, CRM writeback, failure handling, transfer context, and total cost, using acceptance thresholds set for your operation.


## FAQs


**What counts as telephony integration for contact center AI?**
Telephony integration connects an AI agent to a dialer or CCaaS platform for call routing. Evaluate transfers and data exchange separately. SigmaMind AI documents a VICIdial connection and reports support for Five9, NICE, and Genesys, but you must test whether qualification details reach the human agent.


**Do contact center AI platforms replace existing dialers?**
Some platforms provide their own telephony, while others can operate through an existing dialer. SigmaMind AI documents a VICIdial bolt-on that retains the dialer’s campaigns and reports; teams can also evaluate a full migration. Compare the integration and testing required for the bolt-on with the campaign logic, carrier connections, compliance procedures, and reporting that a migration would need to re-create.


**What does contact center AI typically cost per minute?**
Per-minute costs may combine the platform, speech services, language models, and telephony. SigmaMind AI advertises a $0.04-per-minute platform fee with other usage components billed separately, and says it charges no separate concurrency fee. Confirm current plan terms in a quote. Compare complete call costs rather than advertised platform fees alone.


**How should you evaluate CRM sync accuracy?**
CRM sync accuracy measures whether call outcomes and extracted fields reach the correct customer record. Test SigmaMind AI or another platform with real workflows, including transfers and failed calls, and compare the resulting transcripts with CRM records. Check failures and mismatches before enabling CRM writeback in production.
